DAMGHANI:v1p271/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r9.claim: Aṣbar in this phrase expresses boldness: how brazenly they act toward the Fire.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r9.anchor: الثاني الصبر الجرأة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة فما اصبرهم على النار يعني فما اجرأهم على فعل يؤدي بهم الى النار

BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r1.claim: They did not literally buy a price: with respect to this life they gave up guidance for misguidance, and with respect to the next they exchanged forgiveness for punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: بالنسبة إلى الدنيا {الضلالة} التي ليست مما يمكن أن يشتري قطعا

BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r2.claim: ‘How patient they are over the Fire’ marvels at their persistence in deeds that lead to it; Fire names its cause, and the astonishment belongs to human hearers, since divine astonishment would imply ignorance.
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r2.anchor: ما أصبرهم على أعمال أهل النار حين تركوا الهدى وسلكوا مسالك الضلال

BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r3.claim: Their punishment follows because God sent scripture with truth, so rejecting or concealing it and embracing ignorance warrants forms of torment.
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: بسبب أنه {نزل الكتاب} أي : جنس الكتاب

BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r5.claim: The verses severely warn scholars not to hide truth for worldly advantage, fear of losing status, desire for favors or office, or shared attachment to luxury and leadership; such people consume the fire of greed, envy, and desire, which devours good deeds.
BURSEVI:v1p226#2/r5.anchor: لكل من يكتم الحق لغرض فاسد دنيوي

TUSTARI:2:175/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:175/r1.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:2:175/r1.claim: “How patient they are on the Fire” means they dare issue religious judgments without knowledge of the Sunna or law and perform the deeds of Hell's people.
TUSTARI:2:175/r1.anchor: وسئل عن قوله: { فمآ أصبرهم على النار } [175] فقال: أي على الفتوى من غير علم

AKHFASH:v1p166/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p166/r4.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p166/r4.claim: Some take فما أصبرهم على النار as an exclamation of astonishment at them, like قتل الإنسان ما أكفره.
AKHFASH:v1p166/r4.anchor: فزعم بعضهم أنه تعجب منهم كما قال {قتل الإنسان مآ أكفره} تعجبا من كفره.

AKHFASH:v1p166/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p166/r5.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p166/r5.claim: Others read it as a question: what makes them endure the Fire, or what is it that makes them endure it?
AKHFASH:v1p166/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فمآ أصبرهم} أي: ما أصبرهم، و: ما الذي أصبرهم.

FARRA:v1p102#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p102#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p102#2/r5.claim: One reading takes the phrase as asking what made them endure the Fire.

FARRA:v1p102#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p102#2/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p102#2/r6.claim: The other reading is “how bold they are toward the Fire”; the judge's reported idiom ما أصبرك على الله supports this sense.
FARRA:v1p102#2/r6.anchor: قال الكسائي: سألني قاضي اليمن وهو بمكة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r1.claim: ما أصبرهم means “how bold they are toward the Fire.”

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r2.speaker: الكسائي
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī relays a judge's idiom ما أصبرك على الله, said to a man who swore away another's right, as evidence for “how bold.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r2.anchor: عن الكسائي أنه قال: أخبرني قاضي اليمن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid's “how capable they are of the deeds of the people of the Fire” is a good reading, with deeds omitted and endurance understood.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: ما أصبرهم على النار، ما أعملهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes ما as “what thing made them endure the Fire and brought them to it,” not as an exclamation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p69#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: ما أصبرهم على النار.

MAJAZ:v1p64/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p64/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p64/r4.claim: ما is relative here: “what made them endure the Fire and called them to it”; this is not an exclamation.
MAJAZ:v1p64/r4.anchor: «ما» في هذا الموضع في معنى الذي، فمجازها:

IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r1.claim: They chose error over guidance and punishment over forgiveness; Qatada and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas report the same interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : اولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى يقول : اختاروا الضلالة على الهدى ، والعذاب على المغفرة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r2.claim: The exclamation about their endurance means they are remarkably patient and bold in doing the deeds of the people of Hell; several early authorities agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية قوله : فما اصبرهم على النار قال : ما اصبرهم واجراهم على عمل اهل النار

IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r3.claim: Mujahid instead explains the exclamation as how knowledgeable they are about the deeds of the people of Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p286/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد ما اعلمهم باعمال اهل النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r1.claim: Mā aṣbarahum ʿalā al-nār marvels at their endurance of Hell's punishment; certain future suffering is vividly imagined as already witnessed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r1.anchor: تعجيب من شدة صبرهم على عذاب النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r2.claim: This rhetorical presentation makes a future certainty present, as in Zuhayr's and Mālik ibn al-Rayb's poems and the vision of Hell in 102:5–6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p125/r2.anchor: وهذا من طرق جعل المحقق الحصول في المستقبل بمنزلة الحاصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.claim: Choosing misguidance after rejecting accessible guidance is pictured as trade; punishment follows the chosen error and forgiveness would have followed the guidance they discarded, so both are included in the metaphorical purchase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.anchor: ولما كان العذاب تابعا للضلالة التي اشتروها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.claim: Most exegetes take mā aṣbarahum as an exclamation: they are astonishingly fit to remain long in the Fire, as in 80:17 and 19:38.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.anchor: وهو في حيز المخاطبين، أي هم أهل أن تعجبوا منهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن وابن جبير والربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.claim: They explain the exclamation as amazement at the hypocrites' audacity: their behavior shows they have prepared themselves for the Fire and are willing to enter it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.anchor: أظهر التعجب من صبرهم على النار لما عملوا عمل من وطن نفسه عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.speaker: معمر بن المثنى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.claim: Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā reads mā as an interrogative: what has made them endure the Fire? Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers the exclamatory reading clearer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.anchor: استفهام معناه أي شيء أصبرهم على النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.claim: Aṣbara can mean commanding someone to be patient or making someone patient; either sense works if the clause is interrogative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى أصبرهم في اللغة أمرهم بالصبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r1.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls the phrase an interrogative report, not an exclamation, and parses aṣbara as “confined or forced,” citing the prohibition on tormenting a living creature and a poetic line.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r1.anchor: الضبط عند المبرد بضم الهمزة وكسر الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says al-Mubarrad's vowel analysis is wrong: the poetic form is aṣbarahā with fatḥa on hamza and ḍamma on bāʾ, past tense of ṣabara; this undercuts the proposed “make patient” sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p242/r2.anchor: الضبط عند المبرد بضم الهمزة وكسر الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r1.claim: The buyers chose misguidance over guidance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Rabiʿ explain “how patient they are” as patience in deeds that lead them to the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r2.anchor: فما أصبرهم على عمل يؤديهم إلى النار قاله عكرمة والربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid take the phrase to mean how bold they are to face the Fire; al-Kisaʾi cites an Arab’s “How bold you are before God!”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r3.anchor: ما أجرأهم على النار قاله الحسن و مجاهد وذكر الكسائي أن أعرابيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as asking how long they will remain in the Fire, as in asking how long someone endures imprisonment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r4.anchor: ما أبقاهم في النار كما تقول ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says it asks what has made them endure the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r5.anchor: فأي شيء صبرهم على النار قاله ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r6.claim: One grammatical view makes mā interrogative—“what made them patient?”—reported from ʿAta, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r6.anchor: أنها للاستفهام تقديرها ما الذي أصبرهم قاله عطاء والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r7.claim: The alternative makes mā exclamatory, like “how excellent Zayd is”; Ibn al-Anbari says the exclamation is attributed to God to make creatures marvel, not because God marvels as they do.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r7.anchor: أنها للتعجب كقولك ما أحسن زيدا وما أعلم عمرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r8.claim: The verse explains their behavior by saying God sent the Book in truth and those who differed about it are in deep division.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p176#3/r8.anchor: ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتاب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484/r3.claim: They traded away guidance by abandoning scripture's descriptions and good tidings of Muhammad, his mission, and the duty to follow and affirm him; they chose denial and concealment instead, and exchanged forgiveness for punishment and its causes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484/r3.anchor: أي: اعتاضوا عن الهدى، وهو نشر ما في كتبهم من صفة الرسول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r1.claim: The question 'How patient they are with the Fire!' marvels at their endurance of terrible punishment, torment, and shackles, while asking God for protection from it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r1.anchor: يتعجب من رآهم فيها من صبرهم على ذلك، مع (6) شدة ما هم فيه من العذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation is 'How persistent they are in deeds of disobedience that lead them to the Fire.'
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p484#2/r2.anchor: ما أدومهم لعمل المعاصي التي تفضي بهم إلى النار

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r1.speaker: سيبويه والجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r1.claim: ما is a complete indefinite exclamatory noun, not relative or modified: ما أحسن زيدا means something made Zayd beautiful.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r1.anchor: أنها نكرة تامة غير موصولة ولا موصوفة، وأن معناها التعجب

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats ما as interrogative carrying an exclamatory sense, comparable to كيف تكفرون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r2.anchor: أنها استفهامية صحبها معنى التعجب، نحو: كيف تكفرون

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r3.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash is also credited with reading ما as either a relative pronoun or a modified indefinite; these make the clause after it a relative or adjective and require an omitted predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r3.anchor: فإن الجملة بعدها إما صلة أو صفة

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r4.claim: The dispute whether أفعل is noun or verb changes whether its following accusative is a direct object or object-like; the author prefers the verb analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r4.anchor: أهو اسم - وهو قول الكوفيين - أم فعل؟ وهو الصحيح.

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r5.claim: Divine exclamation means informing that their state deserves wonder, not that God experiences wonder; على النار means on the deeds of Hell by metaphor.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r5.anchor: والمراد بالتعجب هنا وفي سائر القرآن الإعلام بحالهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes negative ما, meaning God has not made them patient over the Fire; the author dismisses it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:175/r6.anchor: الخامس: أنها نافية، أي: فما أصبرهم الله على النار، نقله أبو البقاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r7.claim: The people meant are the previously mentioned Jewish scholars, who exchanged unbelief for faith and Hell for Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r7.anchor: يعني من تقدم ذكره من علماء اليهود اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان { والعذاب بالمغفرة } يعني النار بالجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r8.claim: “How patient they are with the Fire!” means how daring they are toward it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r8.anchor: معناه ما أجرأهم على النار , وهذا قول أبي صالح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r9.claim: It may mean how steadfastly they pursue deeds that lead them to the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r9.anchor: فما أصبرهم على عمل يؤدي بهم إلى النار

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r10.claim: It may mean how long He keeps them in the Fire, using ṣabara for keeping someone confined.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r10.anchor: معناه فما أبقاهم على النار , من قولهم : ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r11.claim: The phrase may be an astonished question: what could make them endure the Fire?
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p223#3/r11.anchor: بمعنى أي شيء صبرهم على النار

MUJAHID:v1p94#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p94#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p94#3/r1.claim: He reads فما أصبرهم on the pattern of amazement: how well they act in falsehood.
MUJAHID:v1p94#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾ ما أعملهم بالباطل

MUQATIL:2:174-176/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:174-176/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:174-176/r3.claim: They exchanged their prior faith in Muhammad for denial after his mission and chose punishment over forgiveness; their evil acts make them endure the Fire.
MUQATIL:2:174-176/r3.anchor: يعني باعوا الهدى الذي كانوا فيه من إيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يبعث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r1.claim: They exchanged guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment by concealing the description of Muḥammad.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r1.anchor: يكتمان نعت محمد عليه السلام ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r2.claim: ما أصبرهم is a reproachful question: what makes them endure doing deeds that lead to the Fire?
NASAFI-FULL:v1p85#3/r2.anchor: فأى شيء أصبرهم على عمل يؤدى إلى النار وهذا استفهام معناه التوبيخ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r1.claim: The purchase metaphor extends from their choosing misguidance over guidance to choosing its consequent punishment over forgiveness, since punishment follows misguidance and forgiveness follows the guidance they cast aside.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r1.anchor: ولما كان العذاب تابعا للضلالة وكانت المغفرة تابعة للهدى الذي اطرحوه دخلا في تجوز الشراء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r2.speaker: الجمهور ومنهم الحسن ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r2.claim: They take ما as an exclamation directed at people: marvel at how long the condemned endure in Hell; the construction resembles other Qur'anic exclamations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r2.anchor: مذهب الجمهور منهم الحسن ومجاهد أن «ما» معناه التعجب وهو مردود إلى المخلوقين،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جبير والربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r3.claim: They say the people have no patience for Hell; rather, the phrase means how brazen they are toward it, a known Yemeni expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r3.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وابن جبير والربيع: ما لهم والله عليها من صبر، ولكن ما أجرأهم على النار!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r4.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r4.claim: In al-Farrāʾ's report from him, a Yemeni judge used ما أصبرك على الله to mean how bold you are toward God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: أخبرني الكسائي قال: أخبرني قاضي اليمن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r5.claim: On the boldness reading, their conduct is called courageous because it leads to Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r5.anchor: والمعنى: ما أشجعهم على النار إذ يعملون عملا يؤدي إليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r6.claim: He says ما means what keeps them in the Fire, as in asking what keeps someone in prison.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r6.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أن المعنى ما أبقاهم على النار من قولهم: ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r7.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r7.claim: Another reading makes their lack of distress at Hell into patience, meaning how little they grieve over it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فما أقل جزعهم من النار فجعل قلة الجزع صبرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r8.speaker: الكسائي وقطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r8.claim: They understand the phrase as describing how persistent the condemned are in the deeds of Hell's people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي وقطرب: أي ما أدومهم على عمل أهل النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي وعطاء وأبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r9.claim: They read ما as an interrogative rebuke: what has made them persist in deeds of Hell's people?
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r9.anchor: وقيل: «ما» استفهام معناه التوبيخ قاله ابن عباس والسدي وعطاء وأبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r10.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r10.claim: A further explanation treats the wording as belittling and dismissing them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:175/r10.anchor: وقيل: هذا على وجه الاستهانة بهم والاستخفاف بأمرهم.

RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.claim: In this life knowledge and guidance are best, while ignorance and error are worst; in the next, forgiveness is best and punishment worst, so the concealters are greatest losers in both worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.anchor: أما في الدنيا فأحسن الأشياء الاهتداء والعلم وأقبح الأشياء الضلال والجهل

RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.claim: Because the Jewish scholars knew the truth, the reward for disclosing it, and the punishment for hiding it and spreading doubt, their concealment amounts to exchanging forgiveness for punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.anchor: فلما أقدموا على إخفاء ذلك الحق كانوا بائعين للمغفرة بالعذاب لا محالة

RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r3.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r3.claim: One reading takes the phrase as a rebuking question: what makes them endure the Fire by abandoning truth for falsehood? Ibn al-Anbari notes that af‘ala can mean fa‘ala.
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r3.anchor: أن { ما } في هذه الآية استفهام التوبيخ معناه : ما الذي أصبرهم وأي شيء صبرهم على النار

RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r4.claim: The other reading is an exclamation: knowingly choosing what entails Hell makes them act as if they accept and endure its consequence; the description concerns their present life of moral responsibility.
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r4.anchor: صاروا كالراضين بعذاب الله تعالى ، والصابرين عليه

RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r5.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r5.claim: Al-Asamm says the phrase describes their future silence when ordered to remain in Hell; Razi rejects this as shifting a present description into the future and because the damned may cry out and plead.
RAZI-FULL:v5p25#2/r5.anchor: وقال الأصم : المراد أنه إذا قيل لهم { اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون }

RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r1.claim: Wonder ordinarily combines magnification with an unclear cause, but the word can express magnification alone; divine wonder means magnification, unlike human wonder that involves an unknown cause.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r1.anchor: البحث الأول : في التعجب : وهو استعظام الشيء مع خفاء سبب حصول عظم ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r2.speaker: شريح
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r2.claim: Shurayh rejected the damma reading “I wonder” in 37:12 because ignorance of a cause cannot be attributed to God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r2.anchor: ولهذا أنكر شريح قراءة من قرأ { بل عجبت ويسخرون } ( الصافات : 12 ) بضم التاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r3.speaker: النخعي
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r3.claim: Al-Nakha‘i says divine wonder means sheer magnification; similarly, divine laughter, mockery, and cunning do not have the human meanings of those terms.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r3.anchor: قال النخعي : معنى التعجب في حق الله تعالى مجرد الاستعظام

RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r4.claim: Arabic has two forms of exclamation: ma af‘alahu, as in this verse, and af‘il bihi, as in “How clearly they hear and see!”
RAZI-FULL:v5p26/r4.anchor: للتعجب صيغتين أحدهما : ما أفعله كقوله تعالى : { فما أصبرهم على النار }

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.claim: The fifth argument begins by saying a quality belongs to a thing either intrinsically or through another cause, a premise for rejecting the proposed paraphrase of the exclamation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.anchor: أن كل صفة ثبتت للشيء فثبوتها له إما أن يكون له من نفسه أو من غيره

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r2.claim: They argue that an indefinite noun cannot serve as the subject, so the Basran analysis wrongly makes the most indefinite word a subject.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r2.anchor: المبتدأ لا يجوز أن يكون نكرة فكيف جعلوا ههنا أشد الأشياء تنكيرا مبتدأ

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r3.claim: If “How good Zayd is!” meant “something made Zayd good,” the plain statement should retain the exclamation, but it does not.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r3.anchor: إذا قلنا : شيء حسن زيدا فإنه لا يبقى فيه معنى التعجب ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r4.claim: If God is the one who made Zayd, the sun, moon, and world good, He should be referred to by “who,” not “what”; yet “who made Zayd good” is not an exclamation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز التعبير عنه بما وإن جاز ذلك لكن التعبير عنه سبحانه بمن أولى

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r5.claim: The Basran parsing would make “How good Zayd is!” no different from an ordinary clause such as “Zayd struck Amr,” which has no exclamatory force.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r5.anchor: لا فرق بين قوله : ما أحسن زيدا وبين قوله زيدا ضرب عمرا

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r6.claim: Knowledge that something made Zayd good is necessary, while recognizing an object of wonder is not; thus the proposed paraphrase lacks the exclamation’s meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r6.anchor: فإذن العلم بأن شيئا صيره حسنا علم ضروري والعلم بكونه متعجبا منه غير ضروري

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r7.claim: Their analogy with “a man is writer” is uninformative: everyone knows that some man writes and some cause made Zayd good, so the sentence adds nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r7.anchor: أن في الدنيا رجلا كاتبا فلا يكون هذا الكلام مفيدا

RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r8.claim: The diminutive associated with nouns occurs with ma af‘alahu; if such forms are incompatible with verbs, the formula is not verbal, but if compatible, diminutives should apply to verbs generally, which they do not.
RAZI-FULL:v5p26#2/r8.anchor: دخول التصغير الذي هو من خاصية الأسماء في قولك : ما أحسن زيدا

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r1.claim: The unchanged form of the exclamative supports treating it as a noun: if it were a verb, its middle wāw should shift to alif; the author rejects the appeal to fixed usage.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r1.anchor: تصحيح هذه اللفظة وإبطال إعلاله فإنك تقول في التعجب

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r2.claim: The form cannot be a verb followed by an object because an intervening adverb would then be possible, while the reported usage disallows that separation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r2.anchor: ما أحسن عندك زيدا ، وما أجمل اليوم عبد الله

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r3.claim: Restricting the exclamative pattern to bare triliteral verbs, rather than all transitive verbs, weakens the claim that its first word is an ordinary verb.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r3.anchor: التعجب بكل فعل متعد مجردا كان أو مزيدا

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r4.speaker: البصريون
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r4.claim: The Basrans argue that أحسن is a verb by agreement, so it remains verbal unless evidence redirects it.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r4.anchor: احتج البصريون على أن أحسن في قولنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r5.speaker: البصريون
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r5.claim: The Basrans cite its fixed final fatḥa and the attached accusative pronoun in ما أحسنه as evidence of verbal status.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r5.anchor: أن أحسن مفتوح الآخر ، ولو كان اسما لوجب أن يرتفع

RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r6.claim: The author replies that أحسن can also be a comparative noun and says his multiple arguments against a verb answer the Basrans’ demand for proof.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27/r6.anchor: أحسن كما أنه قد يكون فعلا ، فهو أيضا قد يكون اسما

RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r1.claim: The accusative-pronoun argument for a verb is inconclusive, since the same attachment occurs in لعلني and ليتني; diminutive evidence for nounhood is stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r1.anchor: أنه منتقض بقولك : لعلي وليتني ، والعجب أن الاستدلال بالتصغير

RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes ما as a relative pronoun, أحسن زيدا as its clause, and an omitted predicate; al-Razi calls this weak because the parallel relative sentence is malformed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r2.anchor: القياس أن يجعل المذكور بعد كلمة { ما } وهو قولك : أحسن صلة لما

RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi rejects al-Akhfash’s analysis because الذي أحسن زيدا is not a well-formed sentence, whereas ما أحسن زيدا is complete.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r3.anchor: أنك لو قلت : الذي أحسن زيدا ليس هو بكلام منتظم

RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats ما as interrogative and أفعل as a comparative noun: the question denies that anything is more beautiful than Zayd and challenges an opponent to prove otherwise.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r4.anchor: اختيار الفراء : أن كلمة { ما } للاستفهام وأفعل اسم

RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r5.claim: On al-Farraʾ’s account, أحسن and زيدا take contrasting case endings to distinguish this rhetorical denial from asking which of Zayd’s body parts is best.
RAZI-FULL:v5p27#2/r5.anchor: إلا أنه نصب ليقع الفرق بين ذلك الاستفهام وبين هذا

STUDYQURAN:2:175/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r1.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r1.claim: One interpretation asks what drove them to deeds bringing them nearer the Fire; it is not patience that enables them to endure it.
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r1.anchor: For some, this verse means, “What drove them to the deeds that brought them closer to the Fire?”

STUDYQURAN:2:175/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r2.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r2.claim: Another interpretation asks what gives them patience toward the Fire so that they abandon truth for falsehood.
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r2.anchor: or, “What gives them patience in relation to the Fire so that they abandon truth for falsehood?”

STUDYQURAN:2:175/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r3.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r3.claim: More generally, the phrase is a way of asking what made them do this.
STUDYQURAN:2:175/r3.anchor: In a general sense it can be understood as a way of saying, “What made them do this?”

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r1.claim: The phrase means how brazen they are to perform deeds that bring them near the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r1.anchor: فما أجرأهم على العمل الذي يقربهم إلى النار

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r2.claim: They have no patience for the Fire; the phrase instead marvels at how daring they are toward it.
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r2.anchor: والله ما لهم عليها من صبر، ولكن ما أجرأهم على النار

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير أو بعض أصحابه
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r3.claim: The phrase means how brazen they are toward the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير، أو بعض أصحابه

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r4.claim: They are daring and seemingly patient toward the Fire.

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r5.claim: Another interpretation says they are practiced in falsehood and wrongdoing.

TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r6.claim: The particle ma is interrogative: what could make them endure the Fire?
TAB-FULL:v3p67#3/r6.anchor: هذا على وجه الاستفهام، يقول: ما الذي أصبرهم على النار

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r1.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r1.claim: A question asks what makes them endure the Fire after abandoning truth and following falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r1.anchor: ما يصبرهم على النار حين تركوا الحق واتبعوا الباطل

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r2.claim: He reads the clause as a question, arguing that a statement about patience would have a different case ending.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r2.anchor: هذا استفهام، ولو كانت من الصبر قال

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r3.claim: The question asks what made them persist in the Fire and dare to act as they did.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r3.anchor: ما هذا الذي صبرهم على النار حتى جرأهم

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r4.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن، قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r4.claim: Another view treats the words as an exclamation at their audacity in doing the deeds of those destined for the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r4.anchor: فما أشد جرأتهم على النار بعملهم أعمال أهل النار

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r5.claim: Mujahid also explains the phrase as asking how skilled they are at the deeds of the Fire’s people.

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the exclamation that they are brazen toward the Fire and expert in its people’s deeds; Arabic uses this construction for audacity, and Fire stands for its punishment.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r6.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بتأويل الآية قول من قال: ما أجرأهم على النار،

TAB-FULL:v3p70/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r7.claim: The wonder concerns scholars who concealed Muhammad’s prophethood for bribes despite knowing this would earn God’s anger; mentioning Fire stands for its punishment, as comparisons to Hatim and Antara omit the repeated quality.
TAB-FULL:v3p70/r7.anchor: وإنما معنى ذلك: «فما أجرأهم على عذاب النار»

TABATABAI:2:175/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:175/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:175/r1.claim: The verse depicts deeds taking embodied form: choosing a small price becomes eating fire, then is recast as choosing misguidance over guidance and punishment over forgiveness; their visible persistence is concealment.
TABATABAI:2:175/r1.anchor: ذكر أولا أن اختيارهم الثمن القليل على ما أنزل الله هو أكل النار في بطونهم

TABATABAI:2:175/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:175/r2.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:175/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq interprets “how patient they are with the Fire” as their persistence in doing what they know will lead to it.
TABATABAI:2:175/r2.anchor: قال ما أصبرهم على فعل ما يعلمون أنه يصيرهم إلى النار

TABATABAI:2:175/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:175/r3.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:175/r3.claim: Another report from al-Sadiq reads the phrase as “how bold they are toward the Fire.”

TABATABAI:2:175/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:175/r4.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:175/r4.claim: A third report from al-Sadiq reads it as their diligence in deeds characteristic of the people of the Fire; the author says all three readings are close, the latter two returning to the first sense.
TABATABAI:2:175/r4.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام ما أعملهم بأعمال أهل النار

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r1.claim: Some interpret God’s not speaking to them as a sign of anger, as when one says a person refuses to speak to someone because he is angry.
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r1.anchor:
قال بعضهم معناه يغضب عليهم، كما تقول: فلان لا
يكلم فلانا، تريد هو غضبان عليه.

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God sends no angels to greet them; a further possibility is that He does not let them hear His speech, unlike the righteous.
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم معنى (لا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة) لا يرسل إليهم الملائكة بالتحية،

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r3.claim: ولا يزكيهم means God does not praise them; one whom God does not praise is punished.
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r3.anchor: أي لا يثنى عليهم، ومن لا يثني الله عليه فهو معذب.

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r4.claim: أليم means painful, with مؤلم describing an intensified degree of pain.
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r4.anchor: معنى (أليم) مؤلم ومعنى مؤلم مبالغ في الوجع.

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r5.claim: One reading of فما أصبرهم is ‘what makes them so patient with the Fire?’
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم أي شيء أصبرهم على النار

ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r6.claim: Another reading asks what makes them endure deeds leading to the Fire, though they know opposing the Prophet leads there; ‘what makes him patient against hunger?’ has the same idiom.
ZAJJAJ:v1p245/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: فما أصبرهم على عمل يؤدي إلى النار

TABRISI:2:175/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:175/r1.claim: ما أصبرهم may be an exclamation like the wording in 80:17, meaning they have become an object of astonishment; an Arab saying likewise describes one as patient toward God's punishment.
TABRISI:2:175/r1.anchor: ما أصبرهم قيل إن للتعجب كالتي في قوله:

TABRISI:2:175/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:175/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase asks what makes them endure the Fire; the verb can mean to subject someone to what they dislike, as in al-Ḥuṭayʾa's poem.
TABRISI:2:175/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه للاستفهام على معنى أي شيء أصبرهم

TABRISI:2:175/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:175/r3.claim: The verse refers back to those who traded misguidance for guidance, replacing belief in the Prophet with unbelief.

TABRISI:2:175/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:175/r4.claim: Other interpretations take misguidance as concealing what they knew about the Prophet, or as punishment exchanged for reward and Paradise.
TABRISI:2:175/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد الضلالة كتمان أمره مع علمهم به وبالهدى إظهاره

TABRISI:2:175/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:2:175/r5.claim: Abū Muslim considers “exchanging punishment for forgiveness” a reinforcement of the preceding exchange.
TABRISI:2:175/r5.anchor: قيل إنه تأكيد لما تقدم عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:2:175/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r6.speaker: القاضي
TABRISI:2:175/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī says they knowingly exchanged forgiveness for punishment by persisting in disobedience; al-Ṭabrisī prefers this because it adds a distinct meaning.
TABRISI:2:175/r6.anchor: عن القاضي وهذا أولى لأنه إذا أمكن حمل الكلام على زيادة فائدة كان أولى

TABRISI:2:175/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:2:175/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda take فما أصبرهم as “how audacious they are toward the Fire.”
TABRISI:2:175/r7.anchor: ما أجرأهم على النار ذهب إليه الحسن وقتادة

TABRISI:2:175/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:175/r8.claim: Mujāhid interprets it as “how active they are in deeds of the people of the Fire.”
TABRISI:2:175/r8.anchor: ما أعملهم بأعمال أهل النار عن مجاهد

TABRISI:2:175/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r9.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:175/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj understands the phrase as how long they remain in the Fire, like asking how long someone can endure prison.
TABRISI:2:175/r9.anchor: ما أبقاهم على النار كما يقال ما أصبر فلانا على الحبس عن الزجاج

TABRISI:2:175/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r10.speaker: الكسائي وقطرب
TABRISI:2:175/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Quṭrub read it as how persistent they are in deeds leading to the Fire.
TABRISI:2:175/r10.anchor: ما أدومهم على النار أي ما أدومهم على عمل أهل النار

TABRISI:2:175/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:175/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the wording as an actual question: what keeps them confined to the Fire?
TABRISI:2:175/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن المراد أي شيء أصبرهم على النار

TABRISI:2:175/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:175/r12.claim: Literal divine astonishment is impossible because God knows everything; the exclamation instead makes the unbelievers an object of human amazement, rebuke, and reproach, while the readings can also be understood interrogatively.
TABRISI:2:175/r12.anchor: والتعجب لا يجوز على القديم سبحانه لأنه عالم بجميع الأشياء لا يخفى عليه شيء

TABRISI:2:175/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:175/r13.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:2:175/r13.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls the interrogative reading a good rebuke that makes people marvel at those who freely bring ruin on themselves.
TABRISI:2:175/r13.anchor: وقال المبرد هذا حسن لأنه كالتوبيخ لهم والتعجب لنا

THALABI:v2p47/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p47/r6.claim: They exchanged misguidance for guidance and punishment for forgiveness.
THALABI:v2p47/r6.anchor:
أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة أي استبدلوا الضلالة.
بالهدى

THALABI:v2p47/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والربيع
THALABI:v2p47/r7.claim: For the exclamation reading, they say the verse does not mean the people endure Hell patiently but that they dare to do deeds leading to it; this is Yemeni usage.
THALABI:v2p47/r7.anchor: الحسن وقتادة والربيع: والله ما لهم عليها من صبر ولكن ما أجرأهم على العمل

THALABI:v2p47/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r8.speaker: قاضي اليمن
THALABI:v2p47/r8.claim: A Yemeni judge used the phrase how patient are you with God to mean how daring are you against Him, supporting the boldness interpretation.
THALABI:v2p47/r8.anchor: قاضي اليمن: إن خصمين اختصما إليه فوجبت اليمين على أحدهما فحلف

THALABI:v2p47/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r9.speaker: المورج
THALABI:v2p47/r9.claim: The meaning is how persistent they are in deeds that lead to Hell; they had knowledge, and opposing the Prophet makes a person of Hell.
THALABI:v2p47/r9.anchor: المورج: فما أصبرهم على عمل يؤديهم إلى النار لأن هؤلاء كانوا علماء

THALABI:v2p47/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r10.speaker: الكسائي وقطرب
THALABI:v2p47/r10.claim: They interpret it as how steadfast the people are in the deeds of Hell's inhabitants, like comparing generosity to Hatim's.
THALABI:v2p47/r10.anchor: الكسائي وقطرب: معناه ما أصبرهم على عمل أهل النار أي ما أدومهم عليه

THALABI:v2p47/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r11.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p47/r11.claim: He reads it as sarcasm: how knowledgeable they are about the deeds of Hell's people.
THALABI:v2p47/r11.anchor: مجاهد: ما أعلمهم بأعمال أهل النار

THALABI:v2p47/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p47/r12.claim: Another exclamation means how long God will keep them in the Fire, like asking how long someone bears beating or imprisonment.
THALABI:v2p47/r12.anchor: وقيل: ما أبقاهم في النار! كما يقال: ما أصبر فلانا على الضرب

THALABI:v2p47/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p47/r13.speaker: عطاء والسدي وابن زيد وأبو بكر بن عباس
THALABI:v2p47/r13.claim: They take ma as an interrogative: what made them endure Hell when they abandoned truth and followed falsehood? The question expresses contempt.
THALABI:v2p47/r13.anchor: عطاء والسدي وابن زيد وأبو بكر بن عباس: هي «ما» الاستفهام ومعناه: ما الذي صبرهم وأي شيء صبرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r1.claim: The fa answers the preceding description: those who traded guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment are, by implication, astonishingly patient toward the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r1.anchor: فأما المعنى: ففيه وجهان لأهل التأويل (¬1):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r2.speaker: أهل التأويل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r2.claim: One reported interpretation makes mā exclamatory; the author parses it as a subject, aḥsana as a past-tense verb and predicate, and Zaydan as its object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن (ما) هاهنا تعجب (¬2)، كقولهم: ما أحسن زيدا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r3.claim: Mā is chosen for exclamation because its ambiguity points to the surprising thing; shayʾ could imply belittling it or report a settled fact, whereas an exclamation startles the hearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r3.anchor: وخصت لفظة ما بالتعجب لإبهامها، وهي واقعة على الشيء الذي تتعجب منه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r4.claim: Exclamative aḥsana is a triliteral verb shifted to a quadriliteral form; its fixed final fatḥa shows it is verbal, and the object is accusative because the thing is truly acted upon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r4.anchor: فقد بان بما ذكرنا أن قوله: {فما أصبرهم} إذا # قلنا: إنه تعجب، فعل منقول من الثلاثي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r5.claim: The diminutive mā aḥaysana in poetry does not make the exclamative a noun; it only imitates nouns while remaining a verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p506#2/r5.anchor: وتصغيره لا يدل على أنه اسم، وذلك أن فعل التعجب قد لزم طريقة واحدة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r2.claim: They exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment by rejecting Muhammad’s message and concealing his description.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r2.anchor: حين جحدوا أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وكتموا نعته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r3.claim: “How patient they are with fire” asks what drove them to it by abandoning truth for falsehood; it is a rebuke.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r3.anchor: أي: فأي شيء صبرهم على النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:174-175/r4.claim: An alternative reading is “How audacious they are toward the Fire!”

ELMALILI:2:174-176/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:174-176/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:174-176/r5.claim: The concealers exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment, so misguidance and torment became their lasting acquired possession.
ELMALILI:2:174-176/r5.anchor: dalâlet ve azab onların ebedî milk-i müktesebleri olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:174-176/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:174-176/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:174-176/r6.claim: The exclamation about their patience before the Fire is divine sarcasm: they could not sacrifice worldly pleasure for good, yet persist in deeds that lead to eternal burning and helpless ruin.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r5.claim: By distorting God's verses for worldly gain, they choose misguidance over guidance in this life and punishment over forgiveness and salvation in the next.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r5.anchor: dünyevî bakımdan dalâleti hidayete, uhrevî bakımdan da azabı bağışlanma ve kurtuluşa tercih etmiş bulunmaktadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r6.claim: The closing question asks whether they are so able to endure hellfire that they dared commit such grave sins, delivering a forceful warning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:174/r6.anchor: Onlar cehennem ateşine bu kadar mı dayanıklıdırlar ki böylesine ağır günahları işlemeye cesaret edebilmişlerdir

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p66/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p66/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p66/r1.claim: Qatada explains the question ‘How patient they are toward the Fire!’ as meaning how audacious they are in facing it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p66/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾ قال ما أجرأهم عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r1.claim: Those indicated are the concealors already mentioned; the author does not repeat the explanation of buying misguidance for guidance because it was covered at the beginning of the sūra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r1.anchor: أولئك: اسم إشارة إلى الكاتمين الذين سبق ذكرهم، وذكر ما أوعدوا به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r2.claim: Their worldly exchange of guidance for error ends in an afterlife exchange of forgiveness and eternal bliss for punishment, because they knowingly hid truth for worldly gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r2.anchor: والعذاب بالمغفرة: لما قدم حالهم في الدنيا، بأنهم اعتاضوا من الهدى الضلالة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r3.claim: The verb buy implies preference and desire, since a buyer chooses what he wants; the exchange signals extreme loss and disregard of consequences.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r3.anchor: وفي لفظ اشتروا إشعار بإيثارهم الضلالة والعذاب، لأن الإنسان لا يشتري إلا ما كان له فيه رغبة ومودة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r4.claim: Most commentators read mā in fa-mā aṣbarahum as an exclamation, like the exclamations in 80:17 and 54:31.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r4.anchor: فما أصبرهم على النار: اختلف في ما، فالأظهر أنها تعجبية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r5.claim: On the exclamatory reading, mā is a complete indefinite subject and the following clause is its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r5.anchor: الأول قول سيبويه والجمهور، والثاني قول الفراء وابن درستويه، والثالث والرابع للأخفش.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r6.speaker: الفراء وابن درستويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r6.claim: They analyze mā as interrogative with an exclamatory force, with the following clause as predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r6.anchor: الأول قول سيبويه والجمهور، والثاني قول الفراء وابن درستويه، والثالث والرابع للأخفش.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r7.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r7.claim: One al-Akhfash analysis takes mā as a relative pronoun whose clause is its relative and whose predicate is omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r7.anchor: الأول قول سيبويه والجمهور، والثاني قول الفراء وابن درستويه، والثالث والرابع للأخفش.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r8.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r8.claim: A second al-Akhfash analysis makes mā a described noun, the following clause its description, and leaves the predicate unspoken.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r8.anchor: وكذلك اختلفوا في أفعل بعد ما التعجبية، أهو فعل؟ وهو مذهب البصريين، أم اسم؟ وهو مذهب الكوفيين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r9.speaker: البصريون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r9.claim: Basran grammarians treat the elative after exclamatory mā as a verb, making the following accusative a direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r9.anchor: وكذلك اختلفوا في أفعل بعد ما التعجبية، أهو فعل؟ وهو مذهب البصريين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r10.speaker: الكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r10.claim: Kufan grammarians treat the elative after exclamatory mā as a noun, changing whether its accusative complement is a direct or object-like complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r10.anchor: وكذلك اختلفوا في أفعل بعد ما التعجبية، أهو فعل؟ وهو مذهب البصريين، أم اسم؟ وهو مذهب الكوفيين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r11.claim: Any exclamation of astonishment is attributed to a human observer, since God cannot experience astonishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r11.anchor: وإذا قلنا: إن الكلام هو تعجب، فالتعجب هو استعظام الشيء وخفاء حصول السبب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r12.speaker: الأصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r12.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the damned will truly endure the fire after being silenced and giving up hope of escape.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r12.anchor: فذهب إلى ذلك الأصم وقال: إذا قيل لهم: اخسؤا فيها ولا تكلمون ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r13.claim: The author weakens al-Aṣamm's future-patience reading because the wording appears to describe present patience and people in Hell may show anguish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r13.anchor: وضعف قول الأصم، بأن ظاهر التعجب، أنه من صبرهم في الحال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r14.claim: Another interpretation uses patience figuratively for remaining in the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: الصبر مجاز عن البقاء في النار، أي ما أبقاهم في النار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r15.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r15.claim: Most commentators locate the patience in worldly life; they differ over whether it is literal or metaphorical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r15.anchor: أم هو صبر يوصفون به في الدنيا؟ وهو قول الجمهور. واختلف، أهو حقيقة أم مجاز؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r16.speaker: المؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r16.claim: Al-Muʾarrij takes the patience literally as their persistence in acts leading to Hell despite knowing that defying the Prophet leads there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r16.anchor: والقائلون بأنه حقيقة، قالوا: معناه ما أصبرهم على عمل يؤديهم إلى النار، لأنهم كانوا علماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r17.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r17.claim: One gloss understands aṣbara through a suppressed noun, asking how persistent they are in deeds belonging to Hell's people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p123#2/r17.anchor: وقيل: التقدير ما أصبرهم على عمل أهل النار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r1.speaker: الكسائي عن قاضي اليمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports from al-Kisāʾī that a Yemeni judge used mā aṣbaraka ʿalā Allāh to mean how brazenly a litigant defied God by swearing falsely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: أخبرني الكسائي قال: أخبرني قاضي اليمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses the metaphor as asking how knowledgeable they are about the deeds of Hell's people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r2.anchor: فقيل: هو مجاز أريد به العمل، أي ما أعلمهم بأعمال أهل النار! قاله مجاهد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r3.claim: A further figurative reading asks how little they are distressed by the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز أريد به قلة الجزع، أي ما أقل جزعهم من النار!

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r4.claim: Another figurative reading treats their knowing pursuit of punishment's cause as acceptance of its consequence, like someone exposing himself to a ruler's anger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز أريد به الرضا، وتقريره أن الراضي بالشيء يكون راضيا بمعلوله ولازمه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the exclamation as amazement that they embrace the causes of Hell without caring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فما أصبرهم على النار! تعجب من حالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r6.speaker: معمر بن المثنى والمبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r6.claim: Maʿmar and al-Mubarrad read mā as a rebuking question: what made them endure the fire by abandoning truth for falsehood?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r6.anchor: وذهب معمر بن المثنى والمبرد إلى أن ما استفهامية لا تعجبية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī also hold the interrogative, reproachful reading.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r8.claim: The author says aṣbara means to make someone patient, not the simple verb ṣabara; the hamza is causative, and al-Mubarrad's equation is unattested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r8.anchor: يقال: صبره وأصبره بمعنى: أي جعله يصبر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r9.claim: Some take mā as negation: God does not make them endure punishment; the author summarizes the alternatives as exclamation, interrogation, or negation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p125/r9.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن ما نافية، والمعنى: أن الله ما أصبرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r1.claim: The discourse moves from disbelievers' deafness and blindness to believers' command to eat good food and give thanks, then sets out prohibitions and the necessity exception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر ما هم عليه من الصمم والبكم والعمى، التي هي مانعة من وصول العلوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r4.claim: The condemnation intensifies: they preferred misguidance and punishment, invite amazement at their endurance, and suffer because they opposed the revealed Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p127/r4.anchor: ثم بالغ في ذمهم بأن هؤلاء هم الذين آثروا الضلال على الهدى، والعذاب على النعيم.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r1.claim: Because they concealed truth for low worldly motives, they exchanged guidance for error in this life and forgiveness for punishment in the next; this explains the severe threat against concealers.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r1.anchor: بسبب كتمانهم الحق للمطامع الدنية والأغراض الدنيوية

ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r2.claim: The purchase sentence can stand independently as the answer to why the threat is so severe, or be a second predicate: the first describes threat severity and the second the ugliness of concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r2.anchor: والجملة إما مستأنفة فإنه لما عظم وعيد الكاتمين كان مظنة أن يسأل عن سبب عظم وعيدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r3.claim: 'How patient they are with the Fire!' is a sarcastic wonder for believers at their heedless commission of acts that incur Hell; they are not truly patient.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r3.anchor: أي ما أشد صبرهم وهو تعجب للمؤمنين من إرتكابهم موجباتها من غير مبالاة وإلا فأي صبر لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r4.claim: Most grammarians take mā in the exclamation as a complete indefinite noun in the nominative; al-Farrāʾ treats it as interrogative carrying an exclamatory sense, while al-Akhfash reports relative and indefinite-adjectival analyses.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p44/r4.anchor: في مثل هذا التركيب قيل : نكرة تامة وعليه الجمهور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r1.speaker: عطاء والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r1.claim: They take fa-mā aṣbarahum as a question: what has made them endure the Fire after abandoning truth for falsehood?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r1.anchor: قال عطاء والسدي: هو ما: استفهام معناه ما الذي صبرهم على النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r2.claim: They say the phrase means how brazen they are in doing deeds that bring them toward the Fire; they have no actual patience for it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: والله ما لهم عليها من صبر ولكن ما أجرأهم على العمل الذي يقربهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r3.claim: He reads it as asking how persistently they continue doing the deeds of the people of the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p185/r3.anchor: قال الكسائي: فما أصبرهم على عمل أهل النار أي ما أدومهم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r1.claim: They traded guidance for error in this life and forgiveness for punishment in the next by concealing truth for worldly profits and motives.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r1.anchor: في الدنيا. { والعذاب بالمغفرة } في الآخرة، بكتمان الحق للمطامع والأغراض الدنيوية.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r2.claim: The exclamation marvels at their heedlessness as they become entangled in the causes of Hell without concern.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r2.anchor: تعجب من حالهم في الالتباس بموجبات النار من غيره مبالاة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r3.claim: Mā may be a complete nominative subject, an interrogative followed by its predicate, or a relative pronoun with omitted predicate; poetry illustrates the first construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:175/r3.anchor: وما تامة مرفوعة بالابتداء، وتخصيصها كتخصيص قولهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p320/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p320/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p320/r5.claim: They traded guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment; by concealing knowledge they misled many people and took on their burden as well.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p320/r5.anchor: التي كانت تنجيهم إذا محت صغائرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p321/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p321/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p321/r1.claim: ما أصبرهم can express how tenaciously they imprison themselves in the fire or how brazen they are; if figurative, it resembles threatening a rebel with a long prison sentence and heavy chains.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p321/r1.anchor: وإذا جعلته مجازا كان مثل قولك لمن عاند السلطان

DURR-FULL:v1p405/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p405/r6.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p405/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports ʿAtaʾ's view that the verse describes Jews whom God accuses of concealing scripture in the following verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p405/r6.anchor: عطاء في هذه الآية: هم اليهود الذين أنزل الله فيهم (إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزل الله من الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p409/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r3.claim: They chose misguidance over guidance and punishment over forgiveness; 'how patient they are over the Fire' means how audaciously they act toward it.
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r3.anchor:
عن أبي العالية في قوله {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} الآية
قال: اختاروا الضلالة على الهدى

DURR-FULL:v1p409/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r4.claim: The phrase is not saying they can endure the Fire; it means how daring they are in acts leading to it.
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r4.anchor: في قوله {فما أصبرهم على النار} قال: والله ما لهم عليها من صبر ولكن يقول: ما أجرأهم على النار

DURR-FULL:v1p409/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r5.claim: Qatada explains the phrase as amazement at their audacity in doing what brings them near the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v1p409/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فما أصبرهم} قال: ما أجرأهم على العمل الذي يقربهم إلى النار

DURR-FULL:v1p410/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r1.claim: Al-Suddi reads 'how patient they are over the Fire' as a genuine question: what makes them endure the Fire?
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r1.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {فما أصبرهم على النار} قال: هذا على وجه الاستفهام يقول: ما الذي أصبرهم على النار

DURR-FULL:v1p410/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r2.claim: The people who differed over scripture are Jews and Christians, and their schism is deep enmity.
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r2.anchor: وفي قوله {وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب} قال: هم اليهود والنصارى {لفي شقاق بعيد

DURR-FULL:v1p410/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya condemns disputing the Qur'an, citing the statement that only unbelievers dispute God's signs, and connects this to the distant schism over scripture.
DURR-FULL:v1p410/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: إثنان ما أشدهما علي من يجادل في القرآن (ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r1.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r1.claim: Ibn al-Athir glosses Ali’s phrase about kindling a beacon as displaying a light of truth for its seeker.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r1.anchor: الأثير في حديث الإمام عليّ كرم الله وجهه "حتى أورِىَ قبسا لقابس": أي أظهِر نورا من الحق لطالبه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r2.claim: The lexical entry glosses أليم as painful or aching and cites poetry about pain and sleeplessness as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r2.anchor: وسأله عن معنى قوله تعالى: {لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ} قال: الوجيع، واستشهد بقول الشاعر:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r3.claim: The study notes that descriptions of punishment as painful occur across sixty-eight Quranic verses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p370/r3.anchor: في ثمان وستين آية، وصف فيها عذاب والعذاب، بعذاب أليم، من عذاب أليما، العذاب الأليم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.claim: In the usual Quranic construction, ب marks what is given up in a purchase; thus 2:175 depicts exchanging guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.anchor: يفيد سياقها في تسعة عشر موضعا أنها بمعنى الشراء، والباء فيها دخلت على المبيع المتروك

JISHUMI:v1p485/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p485/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p485/r1.claim: The verse indicates that unbelief is their own act, refuting the Jabriyya.
JISHUMI:v1p485/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن الكفر فعلهم، فيبطل قول الجبرية.

JISHUMI:v1p485/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p485/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p485/r2.claim: Cursing and punishment are deserved through the agent's actions.
JISHUMI:v1p485/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن اللعن والعذاب يستحق بالفعل.

JISHUMI:v1p485/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p485/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p485/r3.claim: A sin committed knowingly is graver, and its perpetrator receives a harsher punishment.
JISHUMI:v1p485/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن الذنب مع العلم أعظم، وعقوبة فاعله أشد.

BAQILLANI:v1p78/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r1.claim: The Qur'an uses the same vivid personifying mode as poetic images of a corner kissing a footprint and a minbar walking toward its addressee; Hell is shown speaking, seeing, and nearly bursting with rage.
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r1.anchor: يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت وتقول هل من مزيد

BAQILLANI:v1p78/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r2.claim: Baqillani calls mumathalah, which Qudama names tamthil, a metaphorical figure opposite irdaf: it compresses an allusion by choosing words that themselves exemplify the intended meaning; this verse is an example.
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r2.anchor: ومن هذا الباب في القرآن قوله

BAQILLANI:v1p78/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r4.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد والأصمعي وعبد الله بن المعتز
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r4.claim: Most authorities define mutabaqa as mentioning a thing together with its opposite, such as night and day or black and white; al-Khalil, al-Asma'i, and Ibn al-Mu'tazz hold this account.
BAQILLANI:v1p78/r4.anchor: ويرون من البديع أيضا ما يسمونه المطابقة وأكثرهم على أن معناها

BURHAN:v1p392/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r1.claim: Mushaf copies vary in the spellings of Harut, Marut, Haman, and Qarun; Dawud keeps its alif because a waw is already omitted, and most copies similarly retain alif in Isra'il after deleting ya.
BURHAN:v1p392/r1.anchor: واختلفت المصاحف فى أربعة هاروت وماروت وهامان وقارون فأما داود فلا خلاف فى رسمه بالألف

BURHAN:v1p392/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r2.claim: Sound masculine and feminine plurals are generally written without alif; the alif remains when a hamza or doubled letter follows it.
BURHAN:v1p392/r2.anchor: وكذلك اتفقوا على حذف الألف فى جمع السلامة مذكرا كان كالعلمين والصبرين والصدقين أو مؤنثا

BURHAN:v1p392/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r3.speaker: ابو العباس
BURHAN:v1p392/r3.claim: Abu al-Abbas explains spelling by whether a quality is viewed from a lower, visible, worldly aspect, which favors retaining alif, or a higher, spiritual aspect, which favors deletion.
BURHAN:v1p392/r3.anchor: قال أبو العباس وقد تكون الصفة ملكوتية روحانية وتعتبر من جهة مرتبة سفلى ملكية هى أظهر فى الاسم

BURHAN:v1p392/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r4.claim: Some orthographic contrasts are transparent, as in the differing treatment of al-akhīr and al-ashrār; other spellings require subtler reflection.
BURHAN:v1p392/r4.anchor: ومنه ما يكون ظاهر الفرقان كالأخير والأشرار تحذف من الأول دون الثانى

BURHAN:v1p392/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r5.claim: In al-firash and al-ta'am, despite similar weight and physical referents, the first is considered through its tangible simile while the second is the tangible food given to the needy.
BURHAN:v1p392/r5.anchor: ومنه ما يخفى كالفراش ويطعمون الطعام فالفراش محسوس والطعام ثابت ووزنهما واحد

BURHAN:v1p392/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r6.claim: In the paired food verse, alif is retained for the People of the Book's food as relatively lower, but omitted for the believers' food as relatively higher because of Islam's superiority.
BURHAN:v1p392/r6.anchor: ثبتت الألف فى الأول لأنه سفلى بالنسبة إلى طعامنا لمكان التشديد عليهم فيه وحذفت من الثانى لأنه علوى

BURHAN:v1p392/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r7.claim: The alif is omitted in “they both ate food” because this food is viewed as higher.

BURHAN:v1p392/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p392/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p392/r8.claim: The doubled form “the doors were shut” conveys intensive action and includes spiritual doors of reliance, so its alif is omitted; singular physical door references distinguish the concrete door.
BURHAN:v1p392/r8.anchor: ليس بمحسوس من أبواب الاعتصام فحذفت الألف لذلك

ITQAN:v1p136/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r1.speaker: النحاة
ITQAN:v1p136/r1.claim: One grammatical interpretation of the seven aḥruf enumerates gender, conditional clauses, inflection, oaths and responses, number, diminutive and augmentative forms, and differing particles.
ITQAN:v1p136/r1.anchor: حكاه عن النحاة وهذا هو الرابع عشر

ITQAN:v1p136/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r2.speaker: الصوفية
ITQAN:v1p136/r2.claim: A Sufi interpretation makes the seven aḥruf seven forms of spiritual conduct, pairing practices such as asceticism, certainty, service, generosity, struggle, fear, hope, gratitude, patience, love, and longing.
ITQAN:v1p136/r2.anchor: حكاه عن الصوفية وهذا هو الخامس عشر

ITQAN:v1p136/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v1p136/r3.claim: A sixteenth interpretation takes the seven aḥruf as seven sciences: creation, divine unity, God's attributes, forgiveness and punishment, resurrection and reckoning, and prophecy.
ITQAN:v1p136/r3.anchor: القول السادس عشر إن المراد بها سبعة علوم علم الإنشاء والإيجاد وعلم التوحيد والتنزيه

ITQAN:v1p136/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r4.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p136/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar relays al-Qurtubi's report from Ibn Hibban that the dispute reached thirty-five views; al-Qurtubi listed five, and Ibn Hajar could not locate Ibn Hibban's account after searching.
ITQAN:v1p136/r4.anchor: وقال ابن حجر ذكر القرطبي عن ابن حبان أنه بلغ الاختلاف في الأحرف السبعة إلى خمسة وثلاثين قولا

ITQAN:v1p136/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p136/r5.claim: Al-Suyuti says Ibn al-Naqib transmits through al-Sharaf al-Mursi Ibn Hibban's statement that scholars differed over the seven aḥruf in thirty-five ways.
ITQAN:v1p136/r5.anchor: قلت قد حكاه ابن النقيب في مقدمة تفسيره عنه بواسطة الشرف المزني المرسي فقال قال ابن حبان

ITQAN:v1p136/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r6.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r6.claim: Ibn Hibban's first view groups exhortation, commands, lawful and forbidden matters, clear and ambiguous verses, and parables.
ITQAN:v1p136/r6.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r7.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r7.claim: His second view lists lawful and forbidden matters, commands, prohibitions, rebuke, reports of future events, and parables.
ITQAN:v1p136/r7.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r8.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r8.claim: His third view comprises promise, threat, lawful and forbidden matters, admonitions, parables, and argument.
ITQAN:v1p136/r8.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r9.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r9.claim: His fourth view comprises commands, prohibitions, glad tidings, warnings, reports, and parables.
ITQAN:v1p136/r9.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r10.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r10.claim: His fifth view lists clear and ambiguous verses, abrogating and abrogated material, particular and general statements, and stories.
ITQAN:v1p136/r10.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r11.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r11.claim: His sixth view comprises commands, prohibitions, encouragement, deterrence, disputation, stories, and parables.
ITQAN:v1p136/r11.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r12.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r12.claim: His seventh view names commands, prohibitions, legal limits, knowledge, secret and manifest meanings, and outward and inward senses.
ITQAN:v1p136/r12.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r13.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r13.claim: His eighth view lists abrogating and abrogated material, promise, threat, rebuke, discipline, and warning.
ITQAN:v1p136/r13.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r14.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r14.claim: His ninth view includes lawful and forbidden matters, openings, reports, virtues, and punishments.
ITQAN:v1p136/r14.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r15.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r15.claim: His tenth view groups commands and warnings, parables, reports, rebuke, exhortation, and stories.
ITQAN:v1p136/r15.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v1p136/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p136/r16.speaker: ابن حبان
ITQAN:v1p136/r16.claim: His eleventh view lists lawful and forbidden matters, parables, explicit texts, stories, and permissions.
ITQAN:v1p136/r16.anchor: قال ابن حبان اختلف أهل العلم في معنى الأحرف السبعة

DAMGHANI:v1p263/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r1.claim: Dāmghānī explains ishtirāʾ as purchase; in the cited 9:111 image, believers have sold themselves to God.
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r1.anchor: الاشتراء الابتياع قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r1.claim: Ṣabr is restraining the self from what it is drawn toward; Ramadan is called the month of patience, and any restraint can be described as ṣabr.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r1.anchor: الصبر : حبس النفس . عما تنازع إليه . وسمي رمضان : شهر [ الصبر ] لذلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r2.claim: A tied animal used as a target and shot until killed is called المصبورة; this practice is prohibited.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r2.anchor: ومنه : المصبورة التي نهي عنها : وهي البهيمة تتخذ غرضا وترمى حتى تقتل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r3.claim: Someone patient through calamity is called ṣābir because he restrains himself from panic.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r3.anchor: وقيل للصابر على المصيبة : صابر لأنه حبس نفسه عن الجزع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari transmits an explanation that patience is named for its bitterness in the heart, like the bitterness of ṣabr in the mouth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r4.anchor: وحكى ابن الأنباري : عن بعض أهل العلم أنه قال : سمي صبر النفوس : صبرا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r5.claim: The most common Qur'anic sense is patience itself, or restraining the self; examples are given in 3:17, 14:21, and 38:44.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r5.anchor: أحدها : الصبر نفسه وهو حبس النفس . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران : ﴿ الصابرين والصادقين ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r6.claim: A second Qur'anic sense is fasting, illustrated by the command to seek help through patience and prayer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r6.anchor: والثاني : الصوم . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في البقرة ) : ﴿ واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets فما أصبرهم على النار as an expression of how daring they are toward the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r7.anchor: والثالث : الجرأة . ومنه قوله تعالى ) فيها : ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾ ، ( أي : فما أجرأهم على النار ) ، ذكره الفراء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r8.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports a Bedouin's rebuke to a liar, ما أصبرك على الله, meaning how audacious you are toward God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p387/r8.anchor: وحكى الأصمعي : أن أعرابيا حلف له رجل كاذب فقال [ له ] الأعرابي ما أصبرك على الله
